title: Trajectory-Constrained Predictive Scaler for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: implement a predictive autoscaling engine for Dedicated fleets that enforces capacity-change trajectories and per-tenant throughput guarantees while respecting safety limits (scale rate, surge budget, and reserved headroom). The engine (TWPS: Time-windowed, Trajectory-constrained Predictive Scaler) combines short-horizon demand forecasts, a constrained optimization-based scale decision, and a backpressure-aware damping stage. TWPS is intended as an alternative to purely reactive quantile/autoregressive scalers for bursty tokenized workloads typical of Redwood customers.
background_and_motivation: We frequently observe oscillation and overshoot when reactive scaling works against bursty tokenized workloads (e.g., short spikes of inference volume). Existing quantile-based autoscalers (percentile targeting + surge credits) are robust but either respond too slowly or overprovision during sustained bursts. TWPS aims to hit throughput SLOs with lower cost by (1) predicting demand across a short control horizon using a lightweight ensemble (EWMA + small AR model seeded from recent windows), (2) enforcing explicit velocity/acceleration constraints on capacity changes (trajectory constraints), and (3) applying safety envelopes for per-tenant guarantees and fleet-level capacity budgets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) TWPS computes scale decisions every 10s using the control horizon of 60s and outputs a target instance count and target throttling plan for each tenant.

2) In canary runs against production-like replay traces, TWPS reduces 95th-tail latency SLO violations by >=20% vs baseline reactive autoscaler for bursty workloads while not increasing average cost by more than 5%.

3) Scaling trajectory constraints enforce max delta+ per-minute <= 30% of active fleet and max absolute scale rate <= 5 instances/min for N-class SKU; violations must be logged and flagged as policy-alerts.
4) Safety fallback: on forecast divergence or sensor gaps, TWPS falls back to current conservative policy (quantile headroom) within 2 control intervals.
5) End-to-end observability: Console shows forecasted throughput, predicted headroom, applied trajectory, rationale reason codes and a linked GitHub PR implementing the controller.
6) Unit + integration tests for forecast model, optimizer, and damping stage with synthetic and recorded traces included in CI.
implementation_notes: Architecture: forecasting (Rust service) -> optimizer (Go microservice) -> executor (existing autoscaler actuator). Forecasts are cached in Redis for 30s.

Optimizer: convex QP formulation (minimize expected SLA penalty + cost subject to linear trajectory constraints). Start with off-the-shelf OSQP; if perf is an issue, fallback to a tuned greedy projection algorithm.
State: use per-tenant 60s sliding windows, feature set = [recent token/sec, recent tail latency, concurrent inflight requests, prefix cache hit rate].
Safety: implement attack surface checks — reject forecasts with insufficient samples and bubble up 'forecast_unreliable' reason.
Controller outputs: desired_instances, preemptive_prefetch_slots, soft_throttle_fraction. Executor must translate desired_instances into scaler API calls with surge-budget accounting.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Forecasting error: overconfident predictions could cause underprovisioning. Mitigation: conservative multiplier on forecasts and aggressive fallback to quantile headroom.
Solver latency: QP solve time must be <50ms at fleet-level. If not, degrade to linear-time projection algorithm with slightly worse optimality.
Complexity vs operability: more knobs increases cognitive load for SREs. Provide sane defaults and automated tuning scripts in Optimize component.
Interference with other policies: TWPS must respect committed capacity and reserved blocks for enterprise customers. Hook into policy-orchestrator for hard constraints.
work_items_and_milestones: WIP-2: Convex optimizer POC using OSQP + translation layer (1w)
WIP-4: Canary pipeline (replay + shadow) + telemetry dashboards (2w)
WIP-5: Safety review + runbook + rollout gating (1w)
WIP-6: Gradual rollout: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks (monitoring gating)
